## VI DRINKING BANNING ORDERS UNDER THE VIOLENT CRIME REDUCTION ACT 2006 19

## Scope of this Section and interpretation

## 65.31

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.31] (1) This Section applies to applications in proceedings in the County Court under sub-sections (2), (3) or (5) of section 4 of the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006 by a relevant authority, and to applications for interim orders under section 9 of that Act. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.31] (2) In this Section –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.31] (a) ‘the 2006 Act’ means the Violent Crime Reduction Act 2006;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.31] (b) ‘relevant authority’ has the same meaning as in section 14(1) of the 2006 Act; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.31] (c) ‘the principal proceedings’ means any proceedings in the County Court. ## Application where the relevant authority is a party in principal proceedings

## 65.32

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.32] (1) Subject to paragraph (2) –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.32] (a) where the relevant authority is the claimant in the principal proceedings, an application under section 4(2) of the 2006 Act for an order under section 4(7) of the 2006 Act must be made in the claim form; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.32] (b) where the relevant authority is a defendant in the principal proceedings, an application for an order must be made by application notice which must be filed with the defence. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.32] (2) Where the relevant authority becomes aware of the circumstances that lead it to apply for an order after its claim is issued or its defence filed, the application must be made by application notice as soon as possible thereafter. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.32] (3) Where the application is made by application notice, it should normally be made on notice to the person against whom the order is sought. ## Application where the relevant authority is not a party in principal proceedings

## 65.33

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.33] (1) Where the relevant authority is not a party to the principal proceedings –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.33] (a) an application under section 4(3) of the 2006 Act to be made a party must be made in accordance with Section I of Part 19; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.33] (b) the application to be made a party and the application for an order under section 4(7) of the 2006 Act must be made in the same application notice. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.33] (2) The applications –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.33] (a) must be made as soon as possible after the relevant authority becomes aware of the principal proceedings; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.33] (b) should normally be made on notice to the person against whom the order is sought. ## Application by a relevant authority to join a person to the principal proceedings

## 65.34

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (1) An application under section 4(5) of the 2006 Act by a relevant authority which is a party to the principal proceedings to join a person to the principal proceedings must be made–

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (a) in accordance with Section I of Part 19;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (b) in the same application notice as the application for an order under section 4(7) of the 2006 Act against the person; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (c) as soon as possible after the relevant authority considers that the criteria in section 4(4) of the 2006 Act are met. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (2) The application notice must contain–

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (a) the relevant authority’s reasons for claiming that the person’s conduct is material in relation to the principal proceedings; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (b) details of the conduct alleged. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.34] (3) The application should normally be made on notice to the person against whom the order is sought. ## Evidence

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > Evidence] 65.35 An application for an order under section 4(7) of the 2006 Act must be accompanied by written evidence, which must include evidence that section 4(6) of the 2006 Act has been complied with. ## Application for an interim order

## 65.36

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] (1) An application for an interim order under section 9 of the 2006 Act must be made in accordance with Part 25. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] (2) The application should normally be made –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] (a) in the claim form or application notice seeking the order; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] (b) on notice to the person against whom the order is sought. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] (3) An application for an interim order may be –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] (a) made without a copy of the application notice being served on the person against whom the order is sought;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] (b) heard in the absence of the person against whom the order is sought,

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.36] with the permission of the court. ## VII PARENTING ORDERS UNDER THE ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR ACT 2003

## Scope of this Section and interpretation

## 65.37

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.37] (1) This Section of this Part applies in relation to applications for parenting orders under sections 26A and 26B of the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003 by a relevant authority. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.37] (2) In this Section –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.37] (a) ‘the 2003 Act’ means the Anti-social Behaviour Act 2003; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.37] (b) ‘relevant authority’ has the same meaning as in section 26C of the 2003 Act. ## Applications for parenting orders

## 65.38

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.38] (1) Subject to paragraph (2) –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.38] (a) where the relevant authority is the claimant in the proceedings, an application for an order under section 26A or 26B of the 2003 Act must be made in the claim form; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.38] (b) where the relevant authority is a defendant in the proceedings, an application for such an order must be made by application notice which must be filed with the defence. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.38] (2) Where the relevant authority becomes aware of the circumstances that lead it to apply for an order after its claim is issued or its defence filed, the application must be made by application notice as soon as possible thereafter. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.38] (3) Where the application is made by application notice, it must normally be made on notice to the person against whom the order is sought. ## Applications by the relevant authority to be joined to proceedings

## 65.39

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.39] (1) Where the relevant authority is not a party to the proceedings –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.39] (a) an application under section 26C(2) of the 2003 Act to be made a party must be made in accordance with Section I of Part 19; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.39] (b) the application to be made a party and the application for an order under section 26A or 26B of the 2003 Act must be made in the same application notice. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.39] (2) The applications –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.39] (a) must be made as soon as possible after the relevant authority becomes aware of the proceedings; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.39] (b) must normally be made on notice to the person against whom the order is sought. ## Applications by the relevant authority to join a parent to proceedings

## 65.40

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (1) An application under section 26C(3) of the 2003 Act by a relevant authority which is a party to the proceedings to join a parent to those proceedings must be made –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (a) in the same application notice as the application for an order under section 26A or 26B of the 2003 Act; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (b) as soon as possible after the relevant authority considers that the grounds for the application are met. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (2) Rule 19.2 does not apply in relation to an application made by a relevant authority under section 26C(3) of the 2003 Act to join a parent to the proceedings. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (3) The application notice must contain–

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (a) the relevant authority’s reasons for claiming the anti-social behaviour of the child or young person is material in relation to the proceedings; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (b) details of the behaviour alleged. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.40] (4) The application must normally be made on notice to the person against whom the order is sought. ## Evidence

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > Evidence] 65.41 An application under section 26A, 26B or 26C of the 2003 Act must be accompanied by written evidence. ## Scope of this Section and interpretation

## 65.42

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.42] (1) This Section applies to applications for an injunction and other related proceedings under Part 4 of the Policing and Crime Act 2009 20 (Injunctions: gang-related violence) and under Part 1 of the Anti-social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014 (Injunctions). [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.42] (2) In this Section—

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.42] (a) ‘the 2009 Act’ means the Policing and Crime Act 2009 21 ; and (b) ‘the 2014 Act’ means the Anti-Social Behaviour, Crime and Policing Act 2014. ## Applications for an injunction

## 65.43

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (1) An application for an injunction under Part 4 of the 2009 Act or Part 1 of the 2014 Act is subject to the Part 8 procedure as modified by this rule and Practice Direction 65. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (2) The application –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (a) must be made by a claim form in accordance with Practice Direction 65;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (b) may be made at any County Court hearing centre;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (c) must be supported by a witness statement which must be filed with the claim form; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (d) must include a statement that the respondent is entitled to a reasonable opportunity to obtain legal representation and to apply for legal aid which may be available without any means test. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (2A) If the application—

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (a) is on notice; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (b) is made at a County Court hearing centre which does not serve the address where—

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (i) the defendant resides or carries on business; or

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (ii) the claimant resides or carries on business,

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] the application will be issued by the County Court hearing centre where the application is made and sent to the hearing centre serving the address at (b)(i) or (ii), as appropriate. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (Practice Direction 65 makes further provision in respect of applications which are not made at the County Court hearing centre which serves the address where the defendant resides or the conduct complained of occurred.)

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (3) The claim form must state–

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (a) the matters required by rule 8.2; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (b) the terms of the injunction applied for. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (4) An application under this rule may be made without notice and where such an application without notice is made–

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (a1) the application may—

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (i) be made at any County Court hearing centre;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (ii) be heard at the hearing centre where the application is made; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (iii) at any stage of the proceedings, be transferred by the court to—

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (aa) the hearing centre which serves the address where the defendant resides or where the conduct complained of occurred; or

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (bb) another hearing centre as the court considers appropriate;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (a) the witness statement in support of the application must state the reasons why notice has not been given; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (b) the following rules do not apply –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (i) 8.3;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (ii) 8.4;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (iii) 8.5(2) to (6);

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (iv) 8.6(1);

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (v) 8.7; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (vi) 8.8. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (5) In every application made on notice, the application notice must be served, together with a copy of the witness statement, by the claimant on the defendant personally. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (6) An application made on notice may be listed for hearing before the expiry of the time for the defendant to file an acknowledgment of service under rule 8.3, and in such a case –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (a) the claimant must serve the application notice and witness statement on the defendant not less than 2 days before the hearing; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.43] (b) the defendant may take part in the hearing whether or not the defendant has filed an acknowledgment of service. ## Injunction containing provisions to which a power of arrest is attached

## 65.44

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (1) In this rule ‘relevant provision’ means a provision of an injunction to which a power of arrest is attached. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (Section 36(6) and (7) and section 40(3) and 41(4) of the 2009 Act and section 4(1)(a) and (b) and (2) of the 2014 Act confer powers to attach a power of arrest to an injunction.)

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (2) Where an injunction contains one or more relevant provisions –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (a) each relevant provision must be set out in a separate paragraph of the injunction; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (b) subject to paragraph (3), the claimant must deliver a copy of the relevant provisions to any police station for the area where the conduct occurred. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (3) Where the injunction has been granted without notice, the claimant must not deliver a copy of the relevant provisions to any police station for the area where the conduct occurred before the defendant has been served with the injunction containing the relevant provisions. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (4) Where an order is made varying or discharging any relevant provision, the claimant must –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (a) immediately inform the police station to which a copy of the relevant provisions was delivered under paragraph (2)(b); and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.44] (b) deliver a copy of the order to any police station so informed. ## Application to vary or discharge an injunction

## 65.45

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.45] (1) An application to vary or discharge an injunction under section 42(1)(b) of the 2009 Act or section 8(1)(a) and (b) of the 2014 Act must be made in accordance with Part 23. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.45] (2) An application by the claimant to vary or discharge the injunction may be made without notice. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.45] (3) If an application under this rule is made without giving notice, the application notice must state the reasons why notice has not been given. ## Application for warrant of arrest under section 44(2) of the 2009 Act or section 10 of the 2014 Act

## 65.46

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.46] (1) An application for a warrant of arrest under section 44(2) of the 2009 Act or section 10 of the 2014 Act must be made in accordance with Part 23 and may be made without notice. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.46] (2) An applicant for a warrant of arrest under section 44(2) of the 2009 Act or section 10 of the 2014 Act must –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.46] (a) file an affidavit setting out grounds for the application with the application notice; or

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.46] (b) give oral evidence of the grounds for the application at the hearing. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.46] (3) Where in accordance with sub-paragraph (2)(b), oral evidence is given, the applicant must produce a written record of that evidence which must be served on the person arrested at the time of the arrest. ## Proceedings following arrest under the 2009 Act and under the 2014 Act(5)

## 65.47

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (1) This rule applies where a person is arrested pursuant to –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (a) a power of arrest attached to a provision of an injunction; or

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (b) a warrant of arrest. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (2) The judge before whom a person is brought following his arrest may –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (a) deal with the matter; or

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (b) adjourn the proceedings. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (3) If proceedings under section 43 or 44 of the 2009 Act or section 9 or 10 of the 2014 Act are adjourned and the arrested person is released –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (a) the matter must be dealt with (whether by the same or another judge) within 28 days of the date on which the arrested person appears in court; and

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (b) the arrested person must be given not less than 2 days’ notice of the hearing. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.47] (4) A contempt application may be issued even if the arrested person is not dealt with within the period in sub-paragraph (3)(a). ## Recognizance

## 65.48

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] (1) Where, in accordance with paragraph 2(2)(b) of Schedule 5 to the 2009 Act or paragraph 2(3)(b) of Schedule 1 to the 2014 Act, the court fixes the amount of any recognizance with a view to it being taken subsequently, the recognizance may be taken by –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] (a) a judge;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] (b) a justice of the peace;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] (c) a justices’ clerk;

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] (d) a police officer of the rank of inspector or above, or in charge of a police station; or

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] (e) where the arrested person is in custody, the governor or keeper of a prison,

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] with the same consequences as if it had been entered into before the court. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.48] (2) The person having custody of an applicant for bail must release that person if satisfied that the required recognizances have been taken. ## Applications for a power of arrest to be attached to any provision of an injunction

## 65.49

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.49] (1) An application under section 34 or 39 of the 2009 Act or section 5 or 6 of the 2014 Act which includes an application for a power of arrest to be attached to any provision of an injunction must be made in the proceedings seeking the injunction by –

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.49] (a) the claim form; or

[PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.49] (b) an application under Part 23. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.49] (2) Every application must be supported by written evidence. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.49] (3) Every application made on notice must be served personally, together with a copy of the written evidence, by the applicant on the person against whom the injunction is sought not less than 2 days before the hearing. [PART 65 – PROCEEDINGS RELATING TO ANTI-SOCIAL BEHAVIOUR AND HARASSMENT > 65.49] (Attention is drawn to rule 25.3(3) – applications without notice.)
